body: If the file is invalid, shouldn't we return `nullptr` and call it a day? Continuing to parse from here might be risky.

Good point. Returning nullptr would make the failure mode explicit and avoid continuing with potentially inconsistent state.
I'll adjust it accordingly.

First, I think this part should emit an error instead of a warning because if the file position isn't moving, it indicates that no data is being read at all. Unlike other warning checking part which are not critical data (metadata) and still can continue parsing

Second, is this part really important ? I noticed an early `file->get_buffer,` so it is guaranteed to have the position moved. Or if it is caused by `file->seek(chunk_end);`, isn't it better to check if `chunksize` is zero early ?

What do you think ?

The forward-progress check is intentional and acts purely as a safety guard against malformed chunks that could otherwise cause an infinite loop.

All structurally critical errors (truncated headers, invalid size fields, invalid channel count, out-of-bounds reads, etc.) already abort parsing via ERR_FAIL_*.
This specific check is not validating structure but ensuring that the loop always makes progress, even in edge cases like zero-sized or corrupted chunks.

Since parsing stops immediately after this condition and we may already have valid data loaded, escalating this to a hard error would be unnecessarily strict. A warning is sufficient here.

I prefer to keep this as a defensive safeguard to prevent potential infinite loops, especially considering future modifications to the chunk handling logic.

Thank you for the feedback so far. To move this PR forward, I see two reasonable ways to handle the stalled parser when encountering malformed WAV chunks, and I’d like to hear which one the Godot maintainers prefer:

Option 1: Defensive Safeguard (Current Implementation)
This keeps a general forward-progress check at the end of the loop as a universal safety net against malformed or zero-sized chunks. It prevents infinite loops while allowing the parser to return already-loaded valid data (graceful degradation).

Option 2: Strict Validation (Hard Error)
We could instead perform an explicit chunksize == 0 check at the start of the loop and escalate this to a full ERR_FAIL return. This would strictly abort parsing on corrupted data and avoid partial returns, aligning with Godot’s usual error standards.

I am happy to implement either approach. If the maintainers prefer the stricter validation path (Option 2), please let me know and I will update the code accordingly with the necessary size checks and error handling.

Which option aligns better with Godot’s error-handling conventions?
